First, as already noted, it explicitly benefits the corporations that own the news networks and the corporations that advertise on them, but that's not all of it. There's another aspect to it all:

It's so obviously destructive that there's no way to actually talk about it and get any of the people to support it.

With most controversial things, there are ways to sell it. One of the simplest is to present it as a partisan issue, so then you immediately get half of the partisan idiots to support it automatically, and generally get the other half to oppose it for all the wrong reasons. All that's necessary to do that is to figure out some angle to make it at least sound like something beneficial (like characterizing a direct transfer of wealth to the insurance industry as "healthcare reform"). But there's no partisan hook to this. There's no way to even pretend that it benefits anyone other than the corporate interests who overtly own the influence of the negotiators. So that means that as more people come to hear about it and come to understand what it's all about, inevitably more people will come to oppose it, since there isn't even a way to con them into supporting it. So the only workable alternative is to just not even mention it and count on it being completed and in place before the bulk of the people who will be affected by it even know what's going on.

So that's exactly what they're doing.
